{{Short description|American educator (1920–1989)}}
'''William V. Mayer''' (March 25, 1920 – June 30, 1989) was an American educator.<ref name=obit>[http://abt.ucpress.edu/content/51/6/332 William V. Mayer]  obituary, The [[American Biology Teacher]], vol 51, no 6, September 1989</ref>

==Career==
He got his A.B. in zoology from the [[University of California]] and his Ph.D. in biology at [[Stanford University]].
During his long teaching career he taught at Stanford University, [[Wayne State University]], the [[University of Southern California]], and the [[University of Colorado, Boulder]]. He was a member of the [[National Association of Biology Teachers]] (NABT) from 1966 to 1989 and served as its president in 1967.<ref>[https://bscs.org/sites/default/files/_media/community/downloads/NABT_75_gala_carlson2.pdf BSCS Executive Directors] Bill Mayer: 2nd Director	of BSCS 1965-1982, NABT President 1967</ref>	

Mayer's central interest was education reform and he worked for national coordination of goals in the teaching of biology.<ref>''[https://doi.org/10.1086/415145 Biology Education in the United States During the Twentieth Century]''  The Quarterly Review of Biology 61, no. 4 (Dec., 1986): 481-507</ref> From 1965 to 1982 he was director of the [[Biological Sciences Curriculum Study]] (BSCS).  While at BSCS he frequently clashed with [[creationists]] in his campaign to promote excellence and integrity in science education.<ref>[https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/411162 review by Kenneth D. Laser] of ''Biology Teachers' Handbook. Biological Sciences Curriculum Study'' The [[Quarterly Review of Biology]], vol 54, no 2, June 1979</ref>  In 1981 he served as a consultant and witness in the landmark Arkansas creation case [[McLean v. Arkansas]].<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20021002092217/http://www.antievolution.org/projects/mclean/new_site/index.htm McLean v. Arkansas Documentation Project: Dr. William Vernon Mayer]}}</ref>

Mayer was a member of The [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]] (CSI), and in April 2011 CSI honored him by including him in its newly created '''Pantheon of Skeptics'''.<ref>[https://www.csicop.org/about/the_pantheon_of_skeptics William V. Mayer biologist] CSI: The Pantheon of Skeptics</ref>

He was the editor of ''Bookwatch Reviews'' published by the [[National Center for Science Education]].

==Works==
* 1973: ''[https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00219266.1973.9653880 The Vicious Circle]'' [[Journal of Biological Education]], vol 7, issue 5, 1973, pp.&nbsp;29–32
* 1978: ''[https://books.google.com/books/about/Biology_teacher_s_handbook.html?id=MNoPAQAAMAAJ Biology teacher's handbook]'' Biological Sciences Curriculum Study, Wiley, October, 1978, {{ISBN|0471019453}}
* 1985: ''[https://www.amazon.com/Biological-Science-Molecular-Approach-Version/dp/0669067695 Biological Science: A Molecular Approach]'' by William V. Mayer, Don E. Meyer & Richard R. Tolman, D C Heath & Co, November 1985, {{ISBN|0669067695}}
* 1988: ''[https://doi.org/10.2307/1310954 Reading beyond the textbook: Great books of biology]'', with Jack L. Carter, [[BioScience]], vol 38, no 7, August 1, 1988, pp.&nbsp;490–492,
